chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s clarification that Satan’s *slutān* (authority) is not inherent or absolute but contingent upon human free will and voluntary submission, a key tenet in Shia theology distinguishing between divine decree and human agency. This narration underscores the principle that believers retain the capacity to resist Satan’s influence through conscious choice, thereby preserving the justice of God in holding individuals accountable for their spiritual state.
